alignments.note: Διώκετε → 'Follow after'. The object τὴν ἀγάπην is accusative, a case English realizes with no preposition, so under rule 106's accusative arm the phrasal 'after' is the verb's own government and stays inside the verb's unit; the noun keeps a bare 'love'.
The ASV gives 'love' no determiner, so the article has nothing to anchor and is its own unrepresented unit under rule 23; rule 21 forbids leaving a bare preposition on it.
δέ → 'yet', the connective the ASV writes for it.

ζηλοῦτε → 'desire earnestly'. One Greek verb rendered by verb plus adverb, both words glossing the lexeme's own sense; rule 66's test heads the unit on 'desire', the word that glosses the verbal root, with 'earnestly' as its intensifying completion.
πνευματικά → 'spiritual', bare adjective; the supplied noun goes to the governing article under rule 102.

The article governs a substantival adjective, so under rules 49 and 102 the supplied nominal 'gifts' is the article's own, leaving πνευματικά a bare 'spiritual'. Rule 11 keeps the ASV's addition markup on 'gifts' as evidence rather than a verdict, and rule 17's generic-noun clause is scoped to anarthrous Greek, so it does not reach a phrase this article governs. Reading 'gifts' as a rule 7 helper on the adjective, with the article unrepresented, is the competing analysis; rule 102's corpus is unanimous the other way.
ἵνα → 'that', the word introducing its English clause under rule 40.
προφητεύητε → 'ye may prophesy'; the subject pronoun and modal auxiliary are inflection-licensed helpers under rules 7 and 9, and rule 9 heads the unit on the lexical verb.

review_notes: All 11 source and 14 target IDs partitioned exactly once.

τήν is unrepresented (no English determiner for 'love') while τά is aligned to the supplied 'gifts' under rule 102 — the difference is that the second article governs a substantival adjective with a supplied nominal, and the first governs an expressed noun the ASV left bare.
'Follow after' kept whole on the verb because the object is accusative (rule 106); the two δέ particles each keep their own connective ('yet', 'but').
